title: Skimming vs Penetration Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 23
description:
Dev wants to sell the Laddoo Lab six-pack at Rs 200 because "we are premium". Arjun wants Rs 80 because "cheap sells". Today it costs Rs 120. Who is right? It depends on what the price must do. In this animated lesson we follow Laddoo Lab, a millet laddoo brand from a home kitchen in Bengaluru, as Zoya decides on a pricing objective before she picks a number.

You will see what a pricing objective and a pricing strategy are, why price is the only part of the marketing mix that brings money in, and a live run of the two classic launch strategies for a new product: market skimming (start high, step down) and market penetration (start low, win buyers fast), with week-by-week buyers. We walk through the five pricing objectives listed by Philip Kotler and Kevin Lane Keller (survival, maximum current profit, maximum market share, market skimming and product quality leadership) with examples from an airline, a hotel, a delivery app, a phone maker and a luxury hotel, and watch Laddoo Lab choose quality leadership and keep the six-pack at Rs 120. We also look at the human side honestly: early buyers can feel cheated when prices fall, price wars hurt small sellers, and India's Competition Act, 2002 bans predatory pricing by a dominant firm.

This is Episode 23 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
